one_liner: Linear-time, non-backtracking C++ regex engine beating classic PCRE on untrusted input; loses to PCRE2 JIT and Hyperscan.
what_it_does: RE2 is a C++ regular expression library with FullMatch/PartialMatch matching plus submatch extraction into std::string/absl::string_view/int, built around a Perl/POSIX-like syntax subset that excludes backreferences and lookaround so every match is guaranteed linear in input length. It is not a drop-in for PCRE: the API (RE2::FullMatch, RE2 objects, RE2::Options) and output types (StringPiece/absl::string_view instead of pcre_exec's ovector) differ, and some patterns will need rewriting. The official Python wrapper ships as google-re2 on PyPI; many other languages have unofficial third-party wrappers.
how_it_is_fast: RE2 compiles a pattern to an automaton and executes it with Thompson-NFA/lazy-DFA style simulation that evaluates all alternatives in parallel instead of backtracking, so match time is asymptotically linear in input length regardless of pattern shape, and there is no catastrophic-backtracking worst case like non-JIT PCRE. It uses no SIMD and no JIT compiler of its own — maintainers closed a request (issue #383) to add x86 SIMD to close the gap with Hyperscan — which is exactly why it loses to PCRE2's JIT and to Hyperscan in the cited benchmark.
when_to_use: Untrusted or user-supplied regex patterns/input where guaranteed linear-time matching (no ReDoS/catastrophic backtracking) is a security requirement.
Serial single-regex matching against classic non-JIT PCRE as the baseline: measured ~3.9x (Talos) and ~2.7x (ET-Open) faster on the NSDI'19 HTTP-traffic benchmark.
C++17+ codebases already depending on Abseil that want a mature (production at Google since 2006), widely used (9.8k stars) engine.
Need safe submatch extraction on adversarial input without recursion/stack-overflow risk.
std::regex is the actual baseline: third-party WG21 paper P1433R0 found RE2 roughly 9x-160x faster than libstdc++/libc++ std::regex on a 1.3GB CSV scan.
when_not_to_use: Need backreferences or lookaround assertions — unsupported by design; a 'bounded lookaround' implementation (issue #585, open since Feb 2026) is only a proof of concept, not merged.

Raw single-regex throughput matters more than backtracking safety and PCRE2 JIT or Hyperscan is available — RE2 lost to PCRE2 10.32 JIT (1777s vs 394s Talos; 4696s vs 913s ET-Open) and to Hyperscan by 9-10x in the same paper.
Extracting many capturing groups per match on a hot path — GitHub issue #204 reports captures making RE2 ~10x slower than non-capturing matches, ending up slower than PCRE with captures on.
Need a PCRE-compatible API/syntax for a true drop-in migration — RE2 requires rewriting call sites and possibly patterns.
Unicode-heavy patterns where compile time matters — issue #46 reports Unicode regex compilation is noticeably slower; RE2 also does no Unicode normalization itself.

integration.form: static lib (also buildable as shared lib via CMake/Bazel, or vendored as source via CMake add_subdirectory)
integration.dependencies: Abseil (required); optional ICU for extended \p/\P Unicode properties (RE2_USE_ICU); GoogleTest + Benchmark needed only to build tests/benchmarks
integration.min_toolchain: C++17; build via GNU make, CMake, or Bazel (Bazelisk); Visual Studio 2019+ on Windows
integration.platforms: any — Linux, macOS, Windows (VS2019+, MinGW, Cygwin/MSYS); no SIMD or specific-arch requirement documented
integration.thread_safety: RE2 objects are documented thread-safe and logically immutable once constructed ('safe for concurrent use by multiple threads', re2.h); LazyRE2 is provided for careful lazy static initialization across threads.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: RE2::FullMatch/PartialMatch and StringPiece/absl::string_view outputs replace PCRE's pcre_exec/ovector, and the syntax subset drops backreferences and lookaround, so call sites and possibly patterns must be rewritten.

gotchas: Capturing submatches is expensive: issue #204 measured captures making RE2 ~10x slower than non-capturing matches (2800ns vs 250ns in that benchmark), ending up slower than PCRE with captures enabled.
No SIMD or JIT of its own, so throughput on modern hardware trails PCRE2 JIT and Hyperscan; maintainers closed a request to add x86 SIMD (issue #383).
Backreferences and lookaround are unsupported by design; 'bounded lookaround' (issue #585) is an open proof-of-concept, not shipped.
No Unicode normalization: a codepoint form and a combining-character form of the 'same' character won't match unless normalized before use (README).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick RE2 over CTRE when the pattern is runtime-supplied or untrusted (user input, config-driven regexes) rather than known at compile time, or when the toolchain is C++17 without C++20; CTRE beats std::regex by ~10x-125x via compile-time NFA generation but requires the pattern to be a compile-time constant, which RE2 does not.
verified_claims_summary: Third-party NSDI'19 Hyperscan paper (Xeon Platinum 8180, single core, GCC 5.4): RE2 serial mode beat JIT-enabled PCRE 8.41 by ~3.9x on Talos (6942s->1777s) and ~2.7x on ET-Open (12800s->4696s), but lost to JIT-enabled PCRE2 10.32 (1777s vs 394s; 4696s vs 913s) and to Hyperscan by ~9-10x; separately, WG21 paper P1433R0 found RE2 far faster than libstdc++/libc++ std::regex on a 1.3GB CSV scan, though with no hardware/flags stated.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-01-22, not archived or a fork), BSD-3-Clause, used in Google production since 2006; not header-only but the source is small and copyable/vendorable via CMake add_subdirectory.
